messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate detected in us-west1 ingress gateway. 5xx% spiked from ~0.5% to ~12% starting ~2026-03-15T14:23Z. Symptoms: HTTP 502/504 and upstream timeouts. Automated page to @sre-oncall and @jordan. Dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/4924689999

sre-oncall: ack — I'm on it. paging rotation: @sre-oncall -> investigating. Can someone tail edge-proxy logs and check upstream error types? :eyes:

jordan: tailing now. `sudo journalctl -u edge-proxy -n 500 | grep -E "502|504|connect_timeout"` shows bursts beginning 14:23Z. Frequent `connect_timeout` to backend-pool-a and a handful of `connection reset by peer` entries.

alex: checking gateway pools/hosts. CPU/mem look okay on gateways. Seeing connection resets from mlworker-01 and mlworker-02 (us-west1). Netstat shows many TIME_WAIT/FIN_WAIT states. Possible conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion. Running: `ss -s` and `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count`.

maria: Support reports customers hitting realtime endpoints with increased error rates (mostly 502). Severity: elevated customer errors (broad but not high throughput loss). Support drafting initial notify.

sre-oncall: quick mitigation options: 1) raise circuit-breaker threshold on ingress to reduce hard fail-fast, 2) steer partial traffic to another region. Recommend immediate partial traffic steer (30%) to us-east1 and enable more aggressive retries. Who can run the steer?

alex: I can run the steer. Executing route steer to shift 30%:  
```
platform-cli traffic steer --from us-west1 --to us-east1 --percent 30 --reason "ingress-5xx-spike"
```

platform-bot: route-steer job accepted (id=rs-4924689999). Estimated convergence ~45s. Audit link: https://platform.redwood.internal/steer/rs-4924689999

jordan: also toggling connection pooling bypass on edge-proxy for backend-pool-a to reduce connection churn while mlworkers recover. Patch applied and edge-proxy restarted on us-west1 gateways:  
```
# edge-proxy config change
backend_pool_a.keepalive: true
systemctl restart edge-proxy
```

sre-oncall: after steer/confg changes, observing 5xx down to ~4% at 14:29Z. Good improvement but still above baseline. Need ml-ops to look at mlworkers and consider recycling nodes showing resets. @ml-ops please?

ml-ops: paged and investigating. I see high socket drops on mlworker-01 (oom? no), kernel logs show `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet`. Looks like conntrack table reached max. Increasing nf_conntrack_raw limit temporarily and scheduling a safe reboot of affected nodes. Applying:  
```
echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```

maria: Support update: initial customer note drafted: "We are investigating elevated error rates in us-west1 and have applied traffic steering and mitigations; some customers may see transient 5xx while we stabilize." Will send after you confirm stabilization. :memo:

alex: performed rolling recycle of mlworker-01 and mlworker-02 (graceful drain, restart, health checks). Health endpoints return 200. Rebalanced backend-pool-a.

jordan: monitoring: 5xx rate back to ~0.6% at 14:41Z, latency returned to baseline. No new conntrack drops after increasing nf_conntrack_max and recycling nodes.

sre-oncall: marking page resolved for now. Recording follow-ups: 1) ml-ops to persist conntrack tuning and add alerts for nf_conntrack utilization, 2) eng-runtime to add earlier fallback to cold pool when backend errors exceed threshold, 3) platform to add a preflight check on route-steer to estimate downstream load.

maria: support will send follow-up customer comms summarizing root cause and mitigations. Draft will be in #support for review.

sre-oncall: creating incident ticket INC-4924689999 and assigning owners for postmortem. Thanks all — great coordination. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=resolved, duration=00:17:35, impact=partial (elevated 5xx/timeouts), postmortem_required=true, incident_link=https://incidents.redwood.internal/4924689999

# post-incident notes (short):  
- probable root cause: conntrack table exhaustion on mlworkers causing upstream resets/timeouts under bursty connection patterns.
- immediate mitigations: increased nf_conntrack_max, recycled affected mlworkers, partial traffic steer to us-east1, enable connection keepalive/pooling on edge-proxy.
- action items: [ml-ops] persist conntrack tuning + test, [eng-runtime] improve fallback logic, [platform] add steer risk estimate, [support] customer comms + monitor.

sre-oncall: locking thread, will append postmortem link when ready."
